body:
The canonical reader consumes some constructors at the wrong native boundary, causing false refusals and acceptance of an invalid program.

```asm
VALUE=2
.byte VALUE .left(.ref(VALUE)+1,{+1})
```

Native ca65 refuses this. We accept it and emit `03`. Changing the count to `.ref(VALUE)` makes native emit `02`, while we refuse it. With a physical operator, `VALUE+.left(.ref(VALUE),{1})`, both correctly emit `03`.

The retained [35-case audit](https://github.com/asm198x/asm198x/tree/b5cec81ae0841737c0d423eee5dd0927a3f13d78/docs/plans/2026-10-21-ca65-constructor-lookahead) records 12 false refusals and three false acceptances across direct/include/macro source. Inactive/unused source and physical-operator controls match. It independently covers generated namespace separators and selector continuation lookahead: native `.byte .left(3,{VALUE,0}) .left(.ref(VALUE),{+1})` emits `0200`, while we refuse it.

Native finishes a scoped name with one token lookahead before referencing the name. A physical operator stops that lookahead; an adjacent constructor runs while the name is finished. Selectors also pre-read and save the caller's current token before pushing their selected list. Our name hook deliberately avoids that constructor lookahead, and selectors push their result without the native continuation pre-read.

Correct those consumption points within #924's approved owned reader. Preserve generated token kinds, the existing scope environment, the shared numeric grammar and caller-token priority. Update the preparation plan's overly strong name-before-all-lookahead claim. Require all 35 controls, every predecessor match, formatter/debug/refusal contracts and lazy-source behavior before qualification. The current reader branch must remain unmerged until this is corrected.
title: ca65 reader misses native constructor lookahead boundaries
